en: back seat (in a bus or classroom)

examples.ko: 뒷자리에 앉은 사람이 큰 소리로 말해요.
examples.en: The person in the back seat talks loudly.
It is hard to see from the back seat in the classroom.
I sat alone in the back seat of the bus.
The back seat was empty, so I moved over there.
Mom put the child in the back seat of the car.
The class was boring, so I talked with the friend in the back seat.

explain: '뒷좌석'은 주로 차 안에서 쓰고, 뒷자리는 교실·버스·극장까지 널리 써요. 반대말은 '앞자리'예요. 학교 이야기에서는 뒷자리가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '뒷좌석' is mostly used inside a car, while 뒷자리 is used widely for classrooms, buses, and theaters too. The opposite is '앞자리'. In stories about school, 뒷자리 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The puppy stands far away and looks at me.
I stepped well back to take a picture.

examples.ko: 불꽃놀이는 멀찍이 앉아서 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to watch fireworks from a seat some distance away.
He stepped far back and watched us.
I parked the car some distance away and walked.
The children threw the ball from a good distance away.

explain: '멀리'보다 '꽤 멀게 떨어져서'라는 느낌이고, 일부러 거리를 둔 것처럼 들릴 때가 많아요. '떨어지다, 서다, 물러나다, 앉다' 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요. '멀찌감치'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '멀리', it gives the feel of 'at a fair distance', and often sounds like keeping distance on purpose. It fits verbs such as 떨어지다, 서다, 물러나다 and 앉다. '멀찌감치' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: It is dangerous to cross the center line when you drive.
A center line is painted in the middle of the road.
The car moved close to the center line.
The center line on Korean roads is usually yellow.
They repainted the center line because of the construction.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 중앙선이 잘 안 보여서 무서워요.
examples.en: When it rains the center line is hard to see, so it is scary.

explain: 중앙선은 노란색이고, 같은 방향으로 가는 차선은 흰색이에요. 중앙선을 넘는 위반은 '중앙선 침범'이라고 부르고, 사고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The center line is yellow, and lines between lanes going the same direction are white. Breaking the rule by crossing it is called '중앙선 침범' (center line violation), which often appears in accident news.

examples.en: Let's meet at the school's back gate.
The back gate closes at six in the evening.
The back gate is close, so I use it often.
If you go out the back entrance, you can see the subway station.
The front gate is good, but the back gate is convenient too.

examples.ko: 공사 중이라 후문을 찾는 손님들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Because of construction, many visitors were looking for the back entrance.

explain: 건물이나 학교의 뒤쪽 출입문을 가리켜요. 짝말은 '정문'이에요. 대학교나 학교 앞에서 '후문에서 만나요'처럼 약속 장소를 정할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the rear entrance of a building or school. Its counterpart is '정문' (main gate). It is also handy for meeting spots, as in '후문에서 만나요'.
